a new patient at The Welcome Practice, there are several things I appreciate and a few important areas that I believe need improvement. I understand that the practice sees many patients daily and that the staff work very hard, but it’s important to share honest feedback so that patient care can continue to improve.

Firstly, the punctuality of the GP practitioners needs urgent improvement. Patients should not be waiting long after their appointment time, especially vulnerable patients. Waiting more than 10 minutes past the scheduled time already feels too long — and during my first new patient appointment, I waited 45 minutes, which is unacceptable. While I understand that some appointments may occasionally run over, such long delays should not be a regular experience. Improving punctuality would greatly improve patient comfort, reassurance, and trust in the service.

Secondly, the admin process needs to be more prompt and consistent. Whether it’s medications, sick notes, prescriptions, or other health issues, practitioners should make sure that patients are offered clear alternatives when something is unavailable or when we are unsure of our options. Communication is key, and patients need to feel fully informed. Ensuring that practitioners take time to understand and prioritise patients’ needs is extremely important, especially for those who are newly registered.

I also feel the practice would benefit from maintaining a calm, supportive, and organised atmosphere. Every patient has different needs and copes differently, and the environment plays a huge part in making people feel safe, respected, and comfortable.

On a very positive note, I want to highlight Amina at reception, who was exceptional. She was caring, helpful, and supportive throughout my registration process. She assisted me with setting up access to my medical records online, answered all my questions at reception, kept me updated about my appointments, and helped with my prescriptions. She is genuinely lovely, and the practice needs more receptionists like her — her kindness and professionalism truly stand out.
